title: Justice on Trial: Why Punishment Doesn’t Heal | Chris Daw KC & Dr Marianne Trent

sentences.zh: 我是临床心理学家玛丽安·特伦特博士，自2019年以来，我一直在通过书籍、

sentences.zh: 我也会参加，支持一个由心理学家组成的可爱社区，共同探索一对一咨询之外的可能性。

sentences.zh: 我叫亚娜，是一名心理健康从业者实习生。

sentences.en: I read the Clinical Psychologist Collective book.
sentences.zh: 我读了《临床心理学家集体》这本书。

sentences.en: I found it really interesting about all the different stories and how people got to become a clinical psychologiSt.
sentences.zh: 我觉得书中关于各种不同故事以及人们如何成为临床心理学家的内容非常有趣。

sentences.en: It just amazed me how many different routes there are to get there and there's no perfect way to become one.
sentences.zh: 通往这一职业的路径之多让我感到惊讶，成为临床心理学家并没有所谓的“完美途径”。

sentences.en: And this kind of filled me with confidence that no, I'm not doing it wrong and put less pressure on myself.
sentences.zh: 这让我充满信心，意识到我并没有走错路，也减轻了我的心理压力。

sentences.en: So if you're feeling a bit uneasy about becoming a clinical psychologist, I'd definitely recommend this just to put yourself at ease and everything will be okay.
sentences.zh: 所以，如果你对成为临床心理学家感到有些不安，我强烈推荐读读这本书，它能让你安心，一切都会好起来的。

sentences.en: But trust me, you will not put the book down once you start.
sentences.zh: 相信我，一旦开始读，你就停不下来了。

sentences.en: Imagine sitting across from someone who's committed a crime and realising the real story isn't about evil, but about trauma.
sentences.zh: 想象一下，坐在一个犯了罪的人对面，意识到他背后的真实故事并非源于邪恶，而是源于创伤。

sentences.en: Today's guest, King's Council Barrister Chris Dorr, has spent decades inside courtrooms
sentences.zh: 今天的嘉宾，御用大律师克里斯·多尔，在法庭和监狱里度过了几十年，

sentences.en: and prisons and what he's learned will completely change how you think about crime, punishment and justice.
sentences.zh: 他所学到的知识将彻底改变你对犯罪、惩罚和正义的看法。

sentences.en: Together, we're exploring the uncomfortable truth that our justice system often punishes pain instead of healing it and why we keep getting that wrong.
sentences.zh: 我们一起探讨了一个令人不安的真相：我们的司法系统往往是在惩罚痛苦，而不是治愈它，以及为什么我们在这方面一直犯错。

sentences.en: Hope you find it super useful.
sentences.zh: 希望你觉得这期节目非常有价值。

sentences.en: I welcome along to the Aspiring Psychologist podcaSt.
sentences.zh: 欢迎来到“有抱负的心理学家”播客。

sentences.en: I'm Dr. Marianne, a qualified clinical psychologiSt.
sentences.zh: 我是玛丽安博士，一名合格的临床心理学家。

sentences.en: And I'm joined here today by Chris Dorr Casey.
sentences.zh: 今天和我一起的是克里斯·多尔·凯西。

sentences.en: Hi, Chris.
sentences.zh: 你好，克里斯。

sentences.en: Welcome along.
sentences.zh: 欢迎来到这里。

sentences.en: Hi.
sentences.zh: 你好。

sentences.en: Well, good morning.
sentences.zh: 早上好。

sentences.en: Thank you so much for being here.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢你能来。

sentences.en: I've followed you like a little LinkedIn creep for probably over five years now.
sentences.zh: 我像个LinkedIn上的小跟踪狂一样关注你大概有五年多了。

sentences.en: And I'm so pleased that you've agreed to come on the podcast because I honestly think everybody
sentences.zh: 我非常高兴你能同意参加这个播客，因为我真心认为每个人

sentences.en: should know about you and about your work and your incredible book, Justice on Trial.
sentences.zh: 都应该了解你、你的工作以及你那本不可思议的书——《审判正义》。

sentences.en: So thank you for being here.
sentences.zh: 所以，谢谢你来到这里。

sentences.en: Not at all.
sentences.zh: 哪里的话。

sentences.en: I'm very excited.
sentences.zh: 我非常兴奋。

sentences.en: And also, my daughter is an aspiring psychologist, so I think I'm in the right place.
sentences.zh: 而且，我的女儿也是一名有抱负的心理学家，所以我想我来对地方了。

sentences.en: Oh, perfect.
sentences.zh: 哦，太完美了。

sentences.en: Well, I didn't know that.
sentences.zh: 我之前还不知道呢。

sentences.en: But yeah, do shove her our way.
sentences.zh: 不过，一定要把她介绍给我们。

sentences.en: So we will go on to think a little bit about what a case even is, but maybe that's not our strongest opener.
sentences.zh: 我们接下来会思考一下什么是“案件”，但这可能不是我们最好的开场白。

sentences.en: Could you tell us a little bit about perhaps why justice is a bit broken, Chris?
sentences.zh: 克里斯，你能告诉我们为什么正义在某种程度上是破碎的吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, I mean, it's because we are obsessed with the idea that you can punish your way out of criminality.
sentences.zh: 是的，这是因为我们沉迷于一种想法，即可以通过惩罚来消除犯罪。

sentences.en: And so we have this kind of ever increasing sort of ratchet effect when it comes to use of incarceration and imprisonment, which, you know, the Americans have taken to the ultimate
sentences.zh: 因此，在监禁和入狱的使用方面，我们有一种不断升级的“棘轮效应”，你知道，美国人已经把这一点发挥到了极致，

sentences.en: degree, almost, of having two and a half million people in their prisons around the U.S.
sentences.zh: 几乎达到了在全美监狱中关押了250万人的程度。

sentences.en: I mean, we're at sort of approaching 100,000.
sentences.zh: 我们这边的人数接近10万。

sentences.en: So even sort of pro rata, we're still not there yet.
sentences.zh: 所以即使按比例计算，我们还没达到那种程度。

sentences.en: But the prison population has doubled in my career of 30 years as a criminal lawyer from sort of mid-40, 90, and then heading towards 100,000.
sentences.zh: 但在我作为刑事律师工作的30年里，监狱人口已经翻了一番，从4万多、9万，现在正朝着10万迈进。

sentences.en: So that it's really that simple.
sentences.zh: 所以事实就是这么简单。

sentences.en: We genuinely as a society, whether we believe it or not, or whether politicians just dissuade us enough that it's a good idea at election time, but we genuinely believe that if you
sentences.zh: 作为一个社会，无论我们是否相信，或者政客们是否在选举时为了说服我们而将其包装成好主意，我们确实认为，如果你

sentences.en: keep on punishing and increasing the amount of time you sentence people to imprison and the length of time they spend in prison, that that's going to magically transform our
sentences.zh: 不断惩罚，不断增加人们的刑期，延长他们在监狱里待的时间，就能奇迹般地将我们的

sentences.en: society into a lower crime society.
sentences.zh: 社会转变为一个低犯罪率的社会。

sentences.en: And somehow or other, it's going to put people off committing crime.
sentences.zh: 并以某种方式阻止人们犯罪。

sentences.en: And, you know, anyone who knows anything about human psychology, and particularly the psychology of those who get themselves caught up in the justice system, in particular when
sentences.zh: 你知道，任何了解人类心理学的人，特别是那些卷入司法系统的人的心理，尤其是当

sentences.en: they're young teenagers, that kind of age, will know that, you know, simply punishing people, relentlessly punishing them more and more, isn't going to solve anything because
sentences.zh: 他们还是十几岁的青少年时，就会知道，仅仅惩罚他们，无休止地加重惩罚，是解决不了任何问题的，因为

sentences.en: the vast majority of the people who are going into prisons have deep-rooted traumas, deep-rooted
sentences.zh: 绝大多数进入监狱的人都有根深蒂固的创伤、根深蒂固的

sentences.en: histories of abuse, you know, in their childhoods or witnessing terrible things happening, or, you know, major psychiatric conditions or addictions and so forth.
sentences.zh: 童年受虐史，或者目睹过可怕的事情发生，或者有严重的精神疾病或成瘾问题等等。

sentences.en: So it's pretty obvious, it seems to me, it's a matter of common sense that you can't imprison
sentences.zh: 所以在我看来，这显而易见，常识告诉我们，你无法通过监禁

sentences.en: your way out of psychological and psychiatric trauma, because, you know, you're just going to make it worse.
sentences.zh: 来解决心理和精神创伤，因为你只会让情况变得更糟。

sentences.en: And therefore, the people who are put through that come out and, on the whole, are even more
sentences.zh: 因此，那些经历过这些的人出来后，总的来说，比进去时更加

sentences.en: broken than when they went in, and sadly, even less likely to be able to engage lawfully in society and productively in society.
sentences.zh: 破碎，遗憾的是，他们更难合法且富有成效地融入社会。

sentences.en: So we just keep making the same mistake.
sentences.zh: 所以我们只是在不断犯同样的错误。

sentences.en: We keep making it in ever greater proportions in the sense that sentences get longer and longer and longer.
sentences.zh: 我们以越来越大的比例重复着这个错误，刑期变得越来越长。

sentences.en: And, you know, it isn't achieving anything except wasting a lot of money and, perhaps even more sadly, wasting a lot of human life.
sentences.zh: 而且，这并没有实现任何目标，除了浪费大量的金钱，更令人悲哀的是，浪费了许多人的生命。

sentences.en: Yeah, I absolutely believe, I agree with everything you're saying.
sentences.zh: 是的，我完全相信，我同意你所说的一切。

sentences.en: And I think there's so many parallels, isn't there?
sentences.zh: 而且我认为有很多相似之处，不是吗？

sentences.en: There's getting tough as a parent, and there's getting tough as a school and dishing out punishments and dishing out, you know, all these detentions.
sentences.zh: 作为父母要“严厉”，作为学校要“严厉”，不断地惩罚，不断地给学生留校察看。

sentences.en: And they just don't mean anything, you know?
sentences.zh: 但这些根本没有任何意义，你知道吗？

sentences.en: It happens so often.
sentences.zh: 这种情况经常发生。

sentences.en: I've seen it.
sentences.zh: 我见过。

sentences.en: I've seen it happening in my own family.
sentences.zh: 我在自己的家庭里也见过。

sentences.en: There's members of, you know, kids in my family, teenagers who have had real troubles at school, and they just keep getting excluded and sent home and told off.
sentences.zh: 我家里的孩子，那些在学校遇到真正麻烦的青少年，他们只是不断地被开除、被送回家、被训斥。

sentences.en: And, you know, it just doesn't work.
sentences.zh: 这根本没用。

sentences.en: I'm not sure what the point of it is, you see?
sentences.zh: 我不确定这样做的意义何在，你明白吗？

sentences.en: I mean, I think the reason I kind of came to writing, and particularly writing Justice on trial, was because I was kind of fed up with just doing the same thing.
sentences.zh: 我想我之所以开始写作，特别是写《审判正义》，是因为我厌倦了总是做同样的事情。

sentences.en: It was like a hamstring in a wheel at work every day, going to court, doing a case, and the process kind of run the system.
sentences.zh: 这就像在工作中每天都在原地踏步，去法庭，处理案件，流程驱动着系统。

sentences.en: So you just do it because that's the system.
sentences.zh: 你只是照做，因为这就是系统。

sentences.en: And then the problem for me is that I started to say to myself, well, we keep doing it, but it's actually, it's making it worse, not better.
sentences.zh: 对我来说，问题在于我开始对自己说，我们一直在做，但实际上情况变得更糟了，而不是更好。

sentences.en: So I took a blank sheet of paper, traveled all over the world, looked at the way that prison
sentences.zh: 所以我拿出一张白纸，走遍世界各地，观察其他国家的监狱

sentences.en: works in other countries, looked at the way that other sort of criminal justice policies operate, and decided to, you know, write a book that just with a blank sheet of paper
sentences.zh: 是如何运作的，观察其他刑事司法政策是如何运作的，并决定写一本书，只用一张白纸

sentences.en: said, this is what you could actually do to make things better, reduce crime, make society
sentences.zh: 写下：你可以做些什么来真正改善现状，减少犯罪，让社会

sentences.en: safer, and save us billions of pounds a year, which all of which seemed like very good ideas
sentences.zh: 更安全，并每年为我们节省数十亿英镑。这些在我看来都是非常好的主意，

sentences.en: to me, none of which are being adopted in any significant way by any government, certainly not in the UK, and certainly not in the US.
sentences.zh: 但没有任何政府以任何实质性的方式采纳它们，在英国肯定没有，在美国也肯定没有。

sentences.en: Well, I think it should be, and, you know, I still think we need to keep beating that drum because I think it's a really inspiring, really interesting book.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我认为应该采纳，而且我认为我们需要继续敲响警钟，因为我认为这是一本非常鼓舞人心、非常有趣的书。

sentences.en: And I think another parallel that's really interesting is you speak about being a very similar age to someone who kind of is really on the wrong tracks and is in all kinds of
sentences.zh: 我认为另一个非常有趣的相似之处是，你谈到自己和一个正处于歧途、陷入各种

sentences.en: strife.
sentences.zh: 困境的人年龄相仿。

sentences.en: And you're almost curious, before we met, we were speaking about the fact that we actually grew up, you know, a few miles away from each other.
sentences.zh: 在见面之前，我们甚至好奇地谈到，我们实际上是在离彼此几英里的地方长大的。

sentences.en: And Milton Keynes is not known for its, you know, its success rates, perhaps, for young people.
sentences.zh: 米尔顿凯恩斯可能并不以年轻人的成功率而闻名。

sentences.en: But you've done, you know, people that are watching on YouTube will be able to see your marvellous garden and hear the birds.
sentences.zh: 但你做得很好，在YouTube上观看的人可以看到你美妙的花园，听到鸟叫声。

sentences.en: People who are listening might be like, what is all that birds?
sentences.zh: 听众可能会想：那些鸟是怎么回事？

sentences.en: Is he recording in an aviary?
sentences.zh: 他是在鸟舍里录音吗？

sentences.en: But, you know, you've done well for yourself.
sentences.zh: 但你确实很有成就。

sentences.en: But you perhaps could have had a different path yourself.
sentences.zh: 不过你本可能走上一条完全不同的道路。

sentences.en: Yeah, I mean, it's an interesting one because, you know, my life kind of took a fork in the road when I was 16.
sentences.zh: 是的，这是一个有趣的话题，因为我的生活在16岁时出现了一个分岔路口。

sentences.en: And it could have taken a completely different fork in the road because
sentences.zh: 它本可以走向一个完全不同的方向，因为

sentences.en: I'd largely been sort of a school refuser, if you like, but not in the sense, I mean, I just bumped off a lot.
sentences.zh: 我基本上算是个“逃学者”，如果可以这么说的话，但我不是那种意义上的逃学，我只是经常旷课。

sentences.en: And back in the 80s, nobody really checked whether you were at school or not.
sentences.zh: 在80年代，没人真的会检查你是否在学校。

sentences.en: Certainly not where I went to school.
sentences.zh: 至少在我上的学校是这样。

sentences.en: I'm sure they did at a lot of schools, but not at mine.
sentences.zh: 我相信很多学校会检查，但我的学校没有。

sentences.en: And so being absent, nobody really cared.
sentences.zh: 所以缺席时，没人真的在乎。

sentences.en: I mean, the schools were so overcrowded.
sentences.zh: 学校太拥挤了。

sentences.en: There were so many kids in the classes.
sentences.zh: 班里有太多的孩子。

sentences.en: The academic attainment was so low that it was kind of like the expectations were just on the floor, which meant that, you know, if you'd even read a book,
sentences.zh: 学术成绩非常低，期望值简直低到尘埃里，这意味着，如果你甚至读过一本书，

sentences.en: that was quite impressive, you know.
sentences.zh: 那都相当令人印象深刻。

sentences.en: And so compared to the education that my kids have, for example, it was completely sort of non-existent in a formal sense.
sentences.zh: 所以与我孩子现在接受的教育相比，那种教育在形式上几乎是不存在的。

sentences.en: But I think because of my personality type, which is quite independent and actually has always been an addictive and obsessive reader, and that was the key.
sentences.zh: 但我认为，由于我的性格类型——相当独立，而且一直是一个沉迷于阅读的人，这就是关键。

sentences.en: So the fact that I read independently from a very young age, my mum taught me to read sort of two, three years of age, even before nursery.
sentences.zh: 我从很小的时候就独立阅读，我妈妈在我两三岁、甚至还没上幼儿园时就教我读书了。

sentences.en: And that, to me, I think is what kind of allowed me later to kind of embark on education and for the first time see the value of education.
sentences.zh: 对我来说，我认为这让我后来能够开始接受教育，并第一次看到了教育的价值。

sentences.en: But that was only because of a set of circumstances that took me to a really good sixth form college when I was 16.
sentences.zh: 但这仅仅是因为一系列机缘巧合，让我在16岁时进入了一所非常好的预科学校。

sentences.en: Whereas had I either stayed in Milton Keynes, where I grew up, or had I, you know, I actually left home to go and sell donuts in the south of
sentences.zh: 如果我留在长大的米尔顿凯恩斯，或者，我实际上在16岁时离家去法国南部的海滩上卖甜甜圈，

sentences.en: France on the beach at the age of 16, had that been a big success, and your listeners may be surprised to know that it wasn't.
sentences.zh: 如果那是一个巨大的成功——听众可能会惊讶地发现它并不是。

sentences.en: But had it been a big success, who knows, I could be the donut king of Nice or something like that instead.
sentences.zh: 但如果它成功了，谁知道呢，我可能现在就是尼斯的甜甜圈大王了。

sentences.en: And I think everybody has these forks in the road, and mine just happened to take me to a good sixth form college.
sentences.zh: 我认为每个人都会遇到这些分岔路口，而我的路口恰好把我带到了一所好的预科学校。

sentences.en: But it took me to a good sixth form college.
sentences.zh: 它把我带到了一所好的预科学校。

sentences.en: And it took me to, ultimately, to Manchester University, which was a great law school, a great university, and of course, an incredible city to live in.
sentences.zh: 最终把我带到了曼彻斯特大学，那是一所很棒的法学院，一所很棒的大学，当然，也是一个生活起来不可思议的城市。

sentences.en: And I ended up spending almost 20 years living and working in Manchester.
sentences.zh: 我最终在曼彻斯特生活和工作了近20年。

sentences.en: And that, to me, was the best thing that could have happened to me.
sentences.zh: 对我来说，那是发生在我身上最好的事情。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And, you know, I think you clearly had family that it was safe to come back to and a safe, stable base.
sentences.zh: 而且，我认为你显然有一个可以安全回归的家庭，一个安全、稳定的基地。

sentences.en: And, you know, you were taught to read.
sentences.zh: 你被教导如何阅读。

sentences.en: And, you know, that was, that wasn't ridiculed, you know, that was seen as actually a good thing for Chris to be doing.
sentences.zh: 那并没有被嘲笑，反而被视为克里斯在做的一件好事。

sentences.en: And a lot of the young people that I work with, for example, in a youth prison, if on the day that you are born or
sentences.zh: 我工作的很多年轻人，例如在青少年监狱里的那些，如果从你出生的那天起，或者

sentences.en: discharged from hospital, you know, your parents leave you in a car seat on the steps of the firehouse
sentences.zh: 从医院出院的那天起，你的父母把你留在消防站台阶上的汽车座椅里，

sentences.en: and go off and do a drugs run, like, your chances to succeed are dramatically reduced, right?
sentences.zh: 然后去跑毒品生意，那么你成功的机会就会大大降低，对吧？

sentences.en: Well, I can tell you, I can tell you a direct story that kind of illustrates that point from my,
sentences.zh: 我可以告诉你一个直接的故事，它说明了这一点，来自我在

sentences.en: my school life in Milton Keynes, because what happened, there was a young boy, I won't give his name, but there's a boy, very young boy, same age as me, who's in my class.
sentences.zh: 米尔顿凯恩斯的学校生活，因为当时班里有一个小男孩，我不说他的名字，但他是一个非常年轻的男孩，和我同龄。

sentences.en: And he always had sort of like clothes that looked like they'd been, I don't know, they didn't fit him.
sentences.zh: 他总是穿着看起来好像……我不知道，不太合身的衣服。

sentences.en: And he always looked very sort of strappy and a bit unkempt and so forth.
sentences.zh: 他看起来总是很邋遢，有点不修边幅等等。

sentences.en: And he got quite badly bullied.
sentences.zh: 他被欺负得很厉害。

sentences.en: And I would sort of chat to him and sort of befriend him a little bit.
sentences.zh: 我会和他聊天，和他交朋友。

sentences.en: And one day I got called into the office at school and asked to come in and Kevin, sorry, I shouldn't give his name, anyway, I'll give his second name.
sentences.zh: 有一天，我被叫到学校办公室，被要求进去，凯文——抱歉，我不该说他的名字，总之，我只说他的姓。

sentences.en: Kevin was in there and he had all his hair had sort of been chopped off.
sentences.zh: 凯文在里面，他的头发被剪得乱七八糟。

sentences.en: And what happened was Kevin had taken some books home from the library and his dad had battered him because he said, why are you wasting your effing time with books?
sentences.zh: 原来凯文从图书馆带了一些书回家，他爸爸狠狠地揍了他，因为他说：“你为什么要把该死的时间浪费在书上？”

sentences.en: You know, you want to do something more useful with your life.
sentences.zh: “你应该做点更有用的事。”

sentences.en: And he cut all his hair off as a punishment for bringing books home.
sentences.zh: 他把凯文的头发全剪了，作为带书回家的惩罚。

sentences.en: So, I mean, if you think about that, I mean, I was very lucky, as you say, my mum was a big reader and still is.
sentences.zh: 所以，如果你想想看，我非常幸运，正如你所说，我妈妈是个大书迷，现在依然是。

sentences.en: And she was obsessed with sort of reading in particular, which I think was her kind of escape from an education that hadn't been particularly successful.
sentences.zh: 她特别沉迷于阅读，我认为这是她逃避那段并不成功的教育经历的方式。

sentences.en: And so she was a sort of self-taught in many ways.
sentences.zh: 所以她在很多方面都是自学的。

sentences.en: And it was only that pure good fortune to have parents who were both encouraging and supportive, but also who were hands-off enough to let me sort of make mistakes, find
sentences.zh: 纯粹的好运让我拥有既鼓励又支持我的父母，而且他们足够放手，让我犯错、自己去发现事物、学习我想学的东西，而不是太执着于我在学校的表现。

sentences.en: things out for myself, learn things that I wanted to learn and weren't too obsessed with what I was doing at school as being the most important thing.
sentences.zh: 他们能看到阅读本身的价值。

sentences.en: They could see that there's value in reading for its own sake.
sentences.zh: 读什么几乎不重要，只要你读了，并且扩展了你的思维和头脑。

sentences.en: And it almost doesn't matter what you read, so long as you read something and you expand your thinking, your mind.
sentences.zh: 所以相比凯文，我非常非常幸运，他仅仅因为从学校带书回家就遭受了身体虐待，命运完全不同。

sentences.en: So very, very lucky in contrast before Kevin, who suffered a completely different fate and was physically abused simply for bringing books home from school.
sentences.zh: 这说明了为什么我们社会中有些人有好运，而另一些人没有，无论金钱或其他因素如何。

sentences.en: And that tells you why some people in our society have good fortune and others don't, regardless of money or anything else.
sentences.zh: 这完全取决于家庭环境，以及是否有对孩子的发展、福利和教育的广泛支持。

sentences.en: It's all to do with that home environment and whether there's a broad kind of support for the child's development and welfare and education.
sentences.zh: 如果有，就像我足够幸运那样，那么即使在表现不佳的地区或学校，

sentences.en: If there is, as I was lucky enough, that was the case for me, then, you know, the potential, even in an area or in a school that's an underperforming school,
sentences.zh: 潜力依然存在。

sentences.en: the potential is still there.
sentences.zh: 但如果你没有任何支持，甚至有反向的阻力，你的人生机会真的会非常非常低。

sentences.en: But if you don't have any of that, and in fact, if you have positive pushback against that, your life chances really are going to be very, very low.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 可怜的凯文。

sentences.en: Poor Kevin.
sentences.zh: 老实说，这简直就像《玛蒂尔达》里的沃姆伍德先生，不是吗？

sentences.en: That is like, honestly, that's like Mr. Wormwood from Matilda, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Like that's Roald Dahl's most horrendous creation, but that's come to real life.
sentences.zh: 那简直是罗尔德·达尔笔下最可怕的创作，但它却在现实生活中上演了。

sentences.en: I was thinking the other day, like my kids don't realise how lucky they are.
sentences.zh: 我前几天还在想，我的孩子们根本没意识到他们有多幸运。

sentences.en: I've got two of them, but they don't realise how lucky they are, that they don't need to be at school wondering what
sentences.zh: 我有两个孩子，但他们没意识到自己有多幸运，他们不需要在学校里担心

sentences.en: mood mummy or daddy's going to be in when they get home or wondering whether mummy's going to be sober.
sentences.zh: 回到家时爸爸妈妈会是什么心情，也不用担心妈妈会不会喝得烂醉。

sentences.en: I actually don't drink at all anymore.
sentences.zh: 其实我现在已经完全不喝酒了。

sentences.en: And that's not because it's been problematic.
sentences.zh: 这并不是因为我有什么酗酒问题。

sentences.en: It's just to think
sentences.zh: 只是觉得

sentences.en: I'm just, I just don't need it.
sentences.zh: 我就是……我根本不需要它。

sentences.en: But, you know, they don't, they don't need to be thinking, oh, has she quit for now?
sentences.zh: 但你知道，他们不需要去想，哦，她这次是戒了吗？

sentences.en: Or has she quit for good?
sentences.zh: 还是彻底戒了？

sentences.en: You know, am I going to have to go home and pick, you know, mop up her vomit?
sentences.zh: 你知道，我回家是不是还得去清理她呕吐的秽物？

sentences.en: Or, you know, how can you be able to learn and to focus on that if you've got all of that in your mind?
sentences.zh: 或者说，如果你的脑子里装满了这些事，你怎么可能静下心来学习和专注呢？

sentences.en: And these are some of the people that you end up working with in the justice system because they're having to be, you know, they've been parentified or they're
sentences.zh: 而这些正是你在司法系统中最终会接触到的人，因为他们不得不……你知道，他们被迫过早承担了父母的责任，或者他们

sentences.en: just having to, I don't know, go out and steal things to even have food to put on the table for their families.
sentences.zh: 只是不得不……我不知道，为了给家里凑出一顿饭，甚至不得不去偷东西。

sentences.en: Like, it just isn't fair, is it?
sentences.zh: 这太不公平了，不是吗？

sentences.en: It's not, it's not, they're not, we're not all starting from the same point in life.
sentences.zh: 确实不公平，我们并非所有人都在人生的同一起跑线上。

sentences.en: No, I mean, and has it ever been any different?
sentences.zh: 不，我是说，这种情况有过改变吗？

sentences.en: I mean, since time began, you know, we've had vast inequalities of wealth, vast inequalities in access to education, vast inequalities in access to health, healthcare and safety.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，自古以来，我们就存在着巨大的贫富差距，在获取教育、医疗和安全保障方面的机会也存在着巨大的不平等。

sentences.en: You know, it's very easy, isn't it, for us in what, the fourth or fifth richest country in the world to get, you know, to kind of come up with these ideas of how awful it is.
sentences.zh: 你知道，对于我们这些生活在世界上第四或第五富有国家的人来说，很容易……很容易产生这种想法，觉得现状有多么糟糕。

sentences.en: And it is awful for many young people in our country.
sentences.zh: 对于我们国家许多年轻人来说，这确实很糟糕。

sentences.en: But if you take a global perspective and you kind of look out a little bit more from our little island and you realise the conditions in which people live in other
sentences.zh: 但如果你从全球视角来看，稍微跳出我们这个小岛，你就会意识到其他国家人们的生活状况，

sentences.en: countries and we're seeing what's happening, you know, in the Middle East and of course, you know,
sentences.zh: 我们看到中东正在发生的事情，当然，还有

sentences.en: extraordinary problems in Africa and South America and all sorts of other places all over the
sentences.zh: 非洲、南美洲以及世界各地其他地方发生的非同寻常的问题，

sentences.en: world where, you know, the levels of inequality, poverty and cruelty towards large sections of the population are so extraordinary as to be unimaginable.
sentences.zh: 在那里，不平等、贫困以及对广大民众的残酷对待，其程度之深简直令人难以想象。

sentences.en: And, you know, I guess in the end, because you can't solve all the problems, you just have to use whatever sort of skill set you have,
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，我想最终因为你无法解决所有问题，你只能利用你所拥有的技能，

sentences.en: whatever knowledge you have to try to make a difference in some way to something.
sentences.zh: 利用你所掌握的知识，去尝试以某种方式带来一点改变。

sentences.en: Because if everyone did that, if everyone did a little bit of something to try and make a little bit of difference, then of course, the cumulative effect would be extraordinary.
sentences.zh: 因为如果每个人都这样做，如果每个人都做一点点努力去尝试带来一点点改变，那么累积起来的效果当然会是惊人的。

sentences.en: The difficulty is that most people, understandably, in many cases, live entirely in their own bubble and totally self-focus on what
sentences.zh: 困难在于，大多数人——在很多情况下是可以理解的——完全生活在自己的泡沫里，完全只关注

sentences.en: their own needs are and their own wants, particularly in wealthy countries.
sentences.zh: 他们自己的需求和欲望，尤其是在富裕国家。

sentences.en: And, you know, in the end, if selfishness is the guiding principle behind most people's lives and most people's sort of outlook,
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，最终如果自私成为大多数人生活和观念背后的指导原则，

sentences.en: then you're going to end up with a selfish and very unequal world and a deeply unfair world.
sentences.zh: 那么你最终会得到一个自私、极度不平等且深感不公的世界。

sentences.en: So to answer your question, yes, it's unfair, but it is, you know, it is inevitable.
sentences.zh: 所以回答你的问题，是的，这不公平，但你知道，这是不可避免的。

sentences.en: There's going to be some level of unfairness.
sentences.zh: 某种程度的不公平总是会存在的。

sentences.en: The question is, what, as an individual, what are you going to do about it?
sentences.zh: 问题是，作为个人，你打算为此做些什么？

sentences.en: Yeah, absolutely.
sentences.zh: 是的，绝对是这样。

sentences.en: It's reminding me of kind of part of our conversation earlier, but also in your book, you speak about the number of incarcerated people in each country actually on paper becomes to
sentences.zh: 这让我想起我们之前谈话的一部分，而且在你的书中，你提到每个国家的监禁人数在纸面上实际上变成了……

sentences.en: be, if you equate it to the number of people in a city, that actually incarceration city is kind of massive and some of the biggest cities in the world.
sentences.zh: 如果你把它等同于一个城市的人口，那么这个“监禁之城”规模巨大，甚至超过了世界上一些最大的城市。

sentences.en: Yeah, well, it was the US in particular that I was talking about.
sentences.zh: 是的，我当时特别提到的是美国。

sentences.en: So if you take that US prison population and give or take two and a half million,
sentences.zh: 所以如果你看看美国的监狱人口，大约是两百五十万左右，

sentences.en: it certainly was that at the time that I wrote the book, then that would have been the fifth largest city in the United States.
sentences.zh: 我写书的时候确实是这个数字，那么它将是美国第五大城市。

sentences.en: I think Houston was fourth and you have New York, LA and Chicago and then
sentences.zh: 我想休斯顿是第四，前面有纽约、洛杉矶和芝加哥，然后是

sentences.en: Houston and then prison and two and a half million people in prison is a quite extraordinary number.
sentences.zh: 休斯顿，再然后就是监狱。两百五十万人被关在监狱里，这是一个相当惊人的数字。

sentences.en: Just to get your head around that number.
sentences.zh: 光是理解这个数字就很不容易。

sentences.en: I mean, that is far bigger than Birmingham, far bigger than Manchester.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这远比伯明翰大，远比曼彻斯特大。

sentences.en: You know, that's an extraordinary number of people.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这是一个惊人的数字。

sentences.en: And, you know, they do live effectively in their, albeit, you know, some of them are in New York and some of them are in
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，他们实际上生活在……虽然，你知道，有些人是在纽约，有些人是在

sentences.en: California, but effectively they all live pretty much in the same basic ecosystem of, you know,
sentences.zh: 加利福尼亚，但实际上他们都生活在基本相同的生态系统中，你知道，

sentences.en: just relentless rolling door incarceration, being constantly on some sort of court supervision,
sentences.zh: 就是那种无休止的、循环往复的监禁，不断地处于某种法院监管之下，

sentences.en: which they can then break and then get sent back to prison and then go again for longer and longer.
sentences.zh: 一旦违反规定，就会被送回监狱，然后刑期越来越长。

sentences.en: You know, it is a quite extraordinary thing to have created a world in which two and a half million people in the richest country in the world are incarcerated.
sentences.zh: 你知道，创造出一个在世界上最富有的国家里有两百五十万人被监禁的世界，这确实是一件非常了不起的事情。

sentences.en: I mean, it's quite extraordinary.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这太惊人了。

sentences.en: Yeah, it really is.
sentences.zh: 是的，确实如此。

sentences.en: And clearly getting tough on crime doesn't work there either.
sentences.zh: 而且很明显，对犯罪采取强硬手段在那里也不管用。

sentences.en: Well, because they're not getting tough on crime.
sentences.zh: 嗯，因为他们并没有对犯罪采取强硬手段。

sentences.en: If you're getting tough on something, say if you want to get tough on cancer, you don't beat the patient with a stick.
sentences.zh: 如果你想对某事采取强硬手段，比如说你想对癌症采取强硬手段，你不会用棍子去打病人。

sentences.en: What you do to get tough on cancer is you find the cleverest medications, the cleverest therapies and the cleverest treatments,
sentences.zh: 要对付癌症，你所做的是寻找最聪明的药物、最聪明的疗法和最聪明的治疗方案，

sentences.en: and you relentlessly apply logic, good practice, pragmatism, and expertise to making, to curing the cancer.
sentences.zh: 并坚持不懈地运用逻辑、良好的实践、务实精神和专业知识来治愈癌症。

sentences.en: You don't simply say, well, this person's got cancer, so we're going to hit them until the cancer's gone.
sentences.zh: 你不会简单地说，好吧，这个人得了癌症，所以我们要打他直到癌症消失。

sentences.en: And that's effectively, metaphorically, what we do with people with our criminal justice system.
sentences.zh: 而这实际上，从隐喻的角度来看，就是我们用刑事司法系统对待人们的方式。

sentences.en: We take people with a serious and significant trauma coming from childhood or coming through their young lives, who then, you know, don't engage properly with education,
sentences.zh: 我们接收那些有着严重且重大的童年创伤或在年轻生活中经历过创伤的人，他们随后，你知道，没有很好地接受教育，

sentences.en: do end up often in the hands of either gangs or other sort of criminal enterprises or sometimes, you know, assisting in crime in some way.
sentences.zh: 最终往往落入帮派或其他犯罪团伙手中，或者有时，你知道，以某种方式协助犯罪。

sentences.en: And then they get themselves arrested, often in their teens, and they get themselves in front of a youth court.
sentences.zh: 然后他们被捕了，通常是在十几岁的时候，然后他们出现在少年法庭上。

sentences.en: Some of them go to young offenders institutions.
sentences.zh: 其中一些人被送进了少年犯管教所。

sentences.en: And essentially, from that point onwards, you may as well tattoo criminal on their
sentences.zh: 从那一刻起，你基本上可以在他们的额头上纹上“罪犯”二字，

sentences.en: forehead, because their life chances are about as high as if you were to wander around looking like that.
sentences.zh: 因为他们的人生机会和你看起来像那样（额头纹字）时差不多高。

sentences.en: And as a society, you know, every time there's an election, you know, we have, you know,
sentences.zh: 作为一个社会，你知道，每次选举的时候，你知道，我们有，你知道，

sentences.en: the government, you know, the parties are arguing about which one's going to lock people up for the longeSt. We're going to give even longer sentences.
sentences.zh: 政府，你知道，各党派在争论谁能把人关得最久。我们要判更长的刑期。

sentences.en: We're going to get tougher.
sentences.zh: 我们要变得更强硬。

sentences.en: But that's the problem.
sentences.zh: 但这就是问题所在。

sentences.en: The terminology of toughness has become completely distorted, because for me, being tough means using your brain power and your energy to aggressively try and solve a problem.
sentences.zh: “强硬”这个词的含义已经被完全扭曲了，因为对我来说，强硬意味着运用你的大脑和精力去积极地尝试解决问题。

sentences.en: That's toughness.
sentences.zh: 那才是强硬。

sentences.en: Toughness is not hitting the most vulnerable people time and time again with long prison sentences at vast
sentences.zh: 强硬不是一次又一次地用长期监禁来打击最脆弱的人群，并耗费巨大的

sentences.en: public expense, only to make the fundamental problem that you're trying to address even worse than it was before you did it.
sentences.zh: 公共开支，结果却让你试图解决的根本问题变得比你干预之前更糟糕。

sentences.en: And at its most simplest, it comes down to, does it not?
sentences.zh: 最简单地说，归根结底，不是吗？

sentences.en: Which is, what's the point of criminal justice?
sentences.zh: 那就是，刑事司法的意义何在？

sentences.en: Why do we have a criminal justice system?
sentences.zh: 我们为什么要设立刑事司法系统？

sentences.en: Now, lots of people, their initial answer would be to punish people who break the law.
sentences.zh: 现在，很多人最初的回答会是：为了惩罚那些触犯法律的人。

sentences.en: That would be their answer.
sentences.zh: 那会是他们的答案。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: The problem with that analysis is, if you do that, what happens next, when you punish the people who broke the law, if you
sentences.zh: 这种分析的问题在于，如果你这样做，接下来会发生什么？当你惩罚了那些触犯法律的人，如果你

sentences.en: punish them in the most aggressive and, you know, they talk about rude, take away their tail of
sentences.zh: 以最激进的方式惩罚他们，你知道，他们谈论粗鲁，拿走他们的电视、游戏机，不让他们拥有这些，让他们单独监禁，24小时，让它变得可怕。

sentences.en: televisions, their face stations, don't let them have all this, make them solitary confinement, 24 hours, make it horrible.
sentences.zh: 这样做的后果是，他们会犯下更多、更久、更严重的罪行。

sentences.en: The consequence of that is that they're going to commit a lot more crimes for a lot longer and a lot worse crime.
sentences.zh: 所以如果你对此感到满意，那就坚持那个不断延长刑期、让监狱条件更严酷的计划吧。

sentences.en: So if you're happy with that, you stick with that plan of just constantly making your sentences longer and your prison conditions harsher.
sentences.zh: 对我来说，你知道，刑事司法系统的目的应该是减少我们现有的犯罪数量，减少

sentences.en: For me, you know, the point of the criminal justice system should be to reduce the amount of crime we have, to reduce the number
sentences.zh: 受害者的数量，特别是像性暴力、身体暴力和家庭暴力等身体伤害犯罪的受害者，

sentences.en: of victims, particularly of physical crimes like sexual violence and physical violence and domestic

sentences.zh: 所以最终，让人们做出选择吧。

sentences.en: And also, you know, would I be petrified at the thought of my kids trying ecstasy in a club?
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，如果想到我的孩子在夜店尝试摇头丸，我会感到恐惧吗？

sentences.en: I'd be more petrified now than I would be if I knew that what the ecstasy they were taking was the dosage was appropriate for their, their height, their weight, their size,
sentences.zh: 我现在会比我知道他们服用的摇头丸剂量适合他们的身高、体重和体型时更恐惧，

sentences.en: and wasn't going to, wasn't going to cause them to end up dead in a hospital.
sentences.zh: 而且不会导致他们死在医院里。

sentences.en: So I'd be much rather they tried something in those circumstances than, for example, in the case of alcohol, you know,
sentences.zh: 所以我宁愿他们在那种情况下尝试某些东西，也不愿像酒精那样，你知道，

sentences.en: tried some illegally made alcohol that had all sorts of stuff in it.
sentences.zh: 尝试一些非法制造的、里面什么都有的酒精。

sentences.en: And who knows what,
sentences.zh: 谁知道里面有什么呢，

sentences.en: I'd much rather they were drinking something that I knew what was in it.
sentences.zh: 我宁愿他们喝的是我知道成分的东西。

sentences.en: And they can make a mistake, they can make mistakes.
sentences.zh: 他们可能会犯错，他们确实会犯错。

sentences.en: And some of them, you know, yes, a proportion of those who use drugs, even in a licensed and legalized market will have a problem with it, undoubtedly.
sentences.zh: 其中一些人，你知道，是的，即使在许可和合法化的市场中，一部分使用毒品的人也会遇到问题，毫无疑问。

sentences.en: But you also then have to ensure that you have, you make accessible, you know, rehab and other forms of sort of
sentences.zh: 但你同时也必须确保你提供了可及的康复中心和其他形式的

sentences.en: therapeutic responses to real drug problems and psychoses, in a way that at the moment, we simply, we under resource all of that provision.
sentences.zh: 针对真正毒品问题和精神病的治疗响应，而目前我们对所有这些服务的投入严重不足。

sentences.en: And many, many of those who have the worst forms of psychological and physical harms from drugs are end up dead.
sentences.zh: 许多因毒品而遭受最严重心理和身体伤害的人最终都死了。

sentences.en: And that to me is an utter tragedy and shows you once again, why the system is so badly broken.
sentences.zh: 对我来说，这完全是一场悲剧，再次向你展示了为什么这个系统如此糟糕地崩溃了。

sentences.en: Yeah, I think when I asked the question, I had forgotten about the licensable bit, I was still thinking about it being legal, but, you know, happening in an underpass.
sentences.zh: 是的，我想当我问那个问题时，我忘记了许可制度的部分，我还在想它只是合法化，但发生在地下通道里。

sentences.en: And that is not what we're talking about.
sentences.zh: 那不是我们在讨论的事情。

sentences.en: Not what I'm advocating, no.
sentences.zh: 那不是我所倡导的，不。

sentences.en: And, you know, anyone who said, make it a free-for-all, let anybody deal any drugs they want.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，任何说“让它完全自由，让任何人想卖什么毒品就卖什么毒品”的人，

sentences.en: I think that's just insane.
sentences.zh: 我觉得那简直是疯了。

sentences.en: That will be even worse, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 那会更糟，不是吗？

sentences.en: Okay, I totally agree.
sentences.zh: 好的，我完全同意。

sentences.en: Just before we finish, in case people are like, I don't even know what a barrister is.
sentences.zh: 在我们结束之前，以防人们像是在问“我甚至不知道什么是大律师（barrister）”。

sentences.en: I don't even know what a KAC is.
sentences.zh: “我甚至不知道什么是御用大律师（KC）”。

sentences.en: Could you give us a very brief overview about what that is, Chris?
sentences.zh: 你能给我们简单介绍一下那是什么吗，克里斯？

sentences.en: Of course.
sentences.zh: 当然。

sentences.en: So in my case, I'm a barrister.
sentences.zh: 在我的职业中，我是一名大律师。

sentences.en: I was called to the bar in 1993.
sentences.zh: 我于1993年获得执业资格。

sentences.en: And that means that you become someone who's entitled to wear a wig and a gown and all the costume that people will have seen on TV and in movies and so forth.
sentences.zh: 这意味着你成为了一名有权佩戴假发和长袍的人，也就是人们在电视和电影中看到的那种装束。

sentences.en: And my job is basically to go to court and act in criminal cases.
sentences.zh: 我的工作基本上是出庭并处理刑事案件。

sentences.en: And in my case, I defend people accused of serious crimes.
sentences.zh: 在我的案例中，我为被指控犯有严重罪行的人辩护。

sentences.en: And I'm, you know, I'm the one that does the trial.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，我就是那个负责审判的人。

sentences.en: I'm the one that cross-examines the witnesses and makes the speeches to the jury and tries to persuade the jury to my side of the case, which in my case is defense.
sentences.zh: 我负责盘问证人，向陪审团发表陈词，并试图说服陪审团站在我这一边，也就是辩方。

sentences.en: I've always done defense.
sentences.zh: 我一直从事辩护工作。

sentences.en: I don't do prosecution cases.
sentences.zh: 我不处理检方案件。

sentences.en: So I'm basically a criminal defense lawyer, trial lawyer.
sentences.zh: 所以我基本上是一名刑事辩护律师、出庭律师。

sentences.en: And a KC is simply the most senior member of the profession of barristers.
sentences.zh: 而KC仅仅是大律师行业中最资深的成员。

sentences.en: And it stands for King's Council.
sentences.zh: 它代表“国王法律顾问”（King's Counsel）。

sentences.en: And it's an appointment which you can apply for.
sentences.zh: 这是一个你可以申请的任命。

sentences.en: Any barrister after a certain period can apply to become a KC.
sentences.zh: 任何大律师在一定年限后都可以申请成为KC。

sentences.en: And if you're appointed, it means that essentially you are in the top 10% in terms of the profession, in terms of quality standards and everything else.
sentences.zh: 如果你被任命，这意味着本质上你处于该行业的前10%，在质量标准和其他各方面都是顶尖的。

sentences.en: So KCs are essentially, as a brand, we are the most
sentences.zh: 所以KC本质上，作为一个品牌，我们是全国最

sentences.en: senior and the most expert barristers or trial lawyers, in my case, in the country.
sentences.zh: 资深、最专业的出庭律师，在我的案例中，是刑事出庭律师。

sentences.en: And our job is, you know, as KCs, we tend to only deal with extremely complex and serious cases.
sentences.zh: 我们的工作是，你知道，作为KC，我们通常只处理极其复杂和严重的案件。

sentences.en: Or in my case, many of my cases are quite high profile cases, actually celebrities or very wealthy people.
sentences.zh: 或者在我的案例中，我的许多案件实际上都是备受瞩目的案件，比如名人或非常富有的人。

sentences.en: And, you know, that's the world in which I operate.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，这就是我所处的领域。

sentences.en: And that's the world that pays for this big garden.
sentences.zh: 这也是支付这个大花园费用的领域。

sentences.en: And it is a beautiful garden.
sentences.zh: 这确实是一个美丽的花园。

sentences.en: I think I've been hearing ladders and tractors and birds.
sentences.zh: 我想我一直听到梯子、拖拉机和鸟叫声。

sentences.en: Like,
sentences.zh: 就像，

sentences.en: there's been a lot going on, but it is...
sentences.zh: 这里发生了很多事情，但它确实……

sentences.en: The gardener decided to bring out his little tractor.
sentences.zh: 园丁决定把他的小拖拉机开出来了。

sentences.en: It is absolutely beautiful.
sentences.zh: 它绝对美丽。

sentences.en: Chris, if people want to learn more about you, your work, your chambers, where's the best place for them to do that?
sentences.zh: 克里斯，如果人们想了解更多关于你、你的工作、你的律师事务所的信息，最好的地方是哪里？

sentences.en: Well, the best place is crystalkc.com, which has got everything about me.
sentences.zh: 嗯，最好的地方是 crystalkc.com，上面有关于我的一切。

sentences.en: It's got all of the different things I do, not just my legal work.
sentences.zh: 它涵盖了我所做的各种事情，不仅仅是我的法律工作。

sentences.en: It has a lot of details, some of the cases I've been involved in, the high profile stuff.
sentences.zh: 里面有很多细节，包括我参与过的一些案件，还有那些备受瞩目的事件。

sentences.en: It has a lot of access to a lot of the writing I've done, journalistic pieces that I've done.
sentences.zh: 它提供了很多我写过的文章，包括我做过的新闻报道。

sentences.en: And it gives you access through to my YouTube channel,
sentences.zh: 它还能让你跳转到我的 YouTube 频道，

sentences.en: Crystal KC's YouTube, which is, has lots of mentoring stuff for young people, career stuff, as well as sort of policy and stuff like that.
sentences.zh: Crystal KC 的 YouTube 频道，上面有很多针对年轻人的指导内容、职业建议，以及一些政策相关的内容等等。

sentences.en: So on the whole, I would just say, go to crystalkc.com and you can also follow me on X and LinkedIn.
sentences.zh: 所以总的来说，我建议你去 crystalkc.com 看看，你也可以在 X 和 LinkedIn 上关注我。

sentences.en: Amazing.
sentences.zh: 太棒了。

sentences.en: I have loved our chat.
sentences.zh: 我很喜欢我们的这次交谈。

sentences.en: It's been five years in the making, but it's been everything I needed it to be and more.
sentences.zh: 这虽然花了五年时间才促成，但它达到了我所期望的一切，甚至更多。

sentences.en: Thank you so much for your time.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢你抽出时间。

sentences.en: I will make sure everything is linked.
sentences.zh: 我会确保把所有链接都放上去。

sentences.en: And I would just like to say, if you found this interesting, please do buy, read, listen to
sentences.zh: 我只想说，如果你觉得这很有趣，请一定要购买、阅读或收听

sentences.en: Crystal Casey's book, which is called Justice on Trial, because it's so interesting.
sentences.zh: Crystal Casey 的书《Justice on Trial》，因为它真的非常有趣。

sentences.en: Thank you so much for your time, Chris.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢你抽出时间，Chris。

sentences.en: No, the talk has been fascinating.
sentences.zh: 不，这次谈话非常引人入胜。

sentences.en: And thank you for being so interested.
sentences.zh: 也谢谢你表现出这么大的兴趣。

sentences.en: And thank you for showing that Milton Keynes can have the odd success story.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你证明了米尔顿凯恩斯也能有出人意料的成功故事。

sentences.en: Yes, indeed it can.
sentences.zh: 是的，确实可以。

sentences.en: Thank you again for your time.
sentences.zh: 再次感谢你抽出时间。

sentences.zh: 非常感谢我们今天这位出色的嘉宾。

sentences.zh: 还有，让我知道你的收获是什么。

sentences.zh: 你知道，作为一个理念，它真的与我产生了共鸣。

sentences.zh: 而且我认为，作为一名临床医生，我自己对创伤非常了解，很难不随处看到创伤的存在。

sentences.zh: 你是怎么想的呢？

sentences.zh: 我想下周我们会有一集，邀请了一位在司法系统工作的临床心理学家，还有她团队的另一位成员，
